examples.prompt: You are stuck in an endless cycle of whenever you die, you will resurrect as a different person in another world and the only way to break the cycle and return home is by destroying the world you are in. The problem? A prophesied hero or group of heroes always rise up to ruin your plans.
examples.response: I died a thousand times across a thousand worlds, only to rise again and shatter each reality with my own hands; yet every time I stood atop the crumbling ruins, a new hero emerged from the ashes to stop me. This time, I targeted a universe where the stars were made of glass, planning to smash the sky and end the cycle forever. But just as my blade struck the celestial dome, a child with a broom swept away my weapon and declared me the villain of the story. The child's laughter triggered a paradox that unraveled my very existence, forcing me back into the void before I could finish my work. I realized too late that the prophecy wasn't about defeating a hero, but about the hero realizing I was the one trapped in the loop.

examples.prompt: Tailor me a story of what it means to be human.
examples.response: A man watched rain fall on his window and felt a sudden, sharp ache in his chest that no machine could replicate. He remembered the warmth of a childhood hug and the sting of a lost love, experiences that defined his fragile existence. Despite knowing he would one day cease to be, he chose to bake bread for a neighbor he barely knew. In that simple act of giving without expectation, he understood the core of his humanity. He smiled at the darkening sky, knowing that to be human is to feel deeply and briefly before fading away.

examples.prompt: A new rule on Earth is made which allows everyone to legally kill 1 person in their life, this affects the world severely & changes how everybody acts.
examples.response: The moment the law was signed, the world held its breath as every citizen quietly selected their one permitted victim; streets emptied not from peace but from the sudden, terrifying clarity of who would be chosen today; a man wept as he pointed a gun at his estranged brother, knowing this was the only time such an act could ever be legal; chaos erupted in markets and homes alike as people rushed to fulfill their quota before the sun set; and in the silence that followed, humanity learned that freedom to kill one person was truly the ultimate curse.
